rationale:
Dawn already reported uncaptured errors and device loss through its own callbacks, but those messages only reached runtime::log_error, so a validation error that dropped a frame never appeared on the timeline beside the frame it killed. A gpu trace category already existed and nothing emitted into it from these paths. This adds instant-event macros to the trace API and a shared sink that the Dawn callbacks feed, keeping their existing log_error calls so nothing that works today regresses. The event name stays an interned StaticString with the message as a debug annotation, because these callbacks run on the render thread and a dynamic name would copy bytes per error. A SkLogHandler subclass feeds the same sink, installing only into an empty handler slot and only when explicitly enabled, so a plugin loaded into a host that already owns Skia's handler never displaces it.

The family is crossed by six paths, all of them the implementation itself: core/render/CMakeLists.txt, core/render/include/pulp/render/gpu_diagnostics.hpp, core/render/src/gpu_compute.cpp, core/render/src/gpu_diagnostics.cpp and core/render/src/gpu_surface_dawn.cpp match core/render/**, and .agents/skills/skia-gpu-build/SKILL.md matches .agents/skills/skia-gpu-build/**. That skill edit records why Pulp now installs an SkLogHandler at all, which the skill previously said was Vellum-owned. Control, run against the same fifteen selectors: core/runtime/include/pulp/runtime/trace.hpp, .agents/skills/trace-analysis/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/trace-sql/SKILL.md, docs/status/gpu-vellum-handoff.yaml and docs/validation/gpu-handoff-provenance/receipt.json match none of them, so the crossing is the render backend and its own skill, not a sweep.

The iOS-Simulator warning filter in gpu_surface_dawn.cpp is preserved byte-identical and still precedes the new emit, so a suppressed Simulator warning produces neither a log nor a trace event. No design-import, packaging, template, release-workflow or installed-SDK-staging changes; no asset changes; no authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a render-backend diagnostics change that crossed its selector.
